content.text: Everything that happened on Day 2 at Augusta NationalThe good times kept rolling for Rory McIlroy after another brilliant day of his Masters title defenseRory McIlroy has made the perfect start to his Masters title defense. Getty ImagesMcIlroy holds record 36-hole leadRory McIlroy will head into the weekend of his Masters title defense with a record six-shot lead.The reigning champion recorded six birdies in his last seven holes to card a 7-under-par 65 and hold the biggest 36-hole lead in Masters history.His closest challengers are Sam Burns and Patrick Reed, who both finished today at 6 under par. Justin Rose, Tommy Fleetwood and Shane Lowry are a shot further back at 5 under par.It was a disastrous end to the day for Bryson DeChambeau whose triple bogey on the 18th green meant he missed the cut for the third time at Augusta National. Scottie Scheffler also scuffled, carding 2-over-par on the day to go to even-par in the tournament. Jon Rahm recovered to 4 under to sneak inside the cut line.
